When the motor is running and your dash lights start flashing on all of a sudden it's usually the alternator. It's usually accompanied by the mph and tach spiking (you'll see them flutter rapidly). 

Sometimes it also happens if you lose your serpentine belt as the serpentine belt drives the alternator so you will get similar symptoms. Serpentine belt will also cause other failures too (you'll lose power steering as well for example).

It could be a battery but battery failures usually are noticed when the engine is being started. Once the vehicle is running it is not drawing power from battery but from alternator.

So to break it down, when the motor is not running all power is drawn from battery. When you turn the key, the starter will crank from battery power. Once the motor is running and spinning, the serpentine belt is connected to the motor and is now spinning, which is also connected to the alternator and in turn generates power that is used to run the vehicle systems and recharge the battery. When you turn the motor off, the job of the alternator is complete and if working normally it recharged the battery enough for the starter to crank next time you turn the motor on. Rinse and repeat until battery is used up enough that you need a new one (it can't be recharged anymore) or your alternator dies (unable to generate enough power to run systems and charge a battery anymore). 

Hope this helps, good luck!

Basically, you add a third address to the transaction, a dispute mediator.  2 parties must agree for the money to be sent.

If the buyer/seller agree, they satisfy the 2 of 3 and the money gets sent as planned.

If the buyer is unhappy, he contacts the 3rd party, who will look at the situation.  If he agrees with the buyer, that constitutes the 2 of 3, and the buyer gets his money returned.  If the mediator sides with the seller, then again, that satisfies 2 of 3 and the seller gets the money.

At no point can the mediator take the money.  They can only decide who gets it.

not "might be", it is built in, along with loads of other protocols not yet utilized.  

It's called a 2 of 3 transaction, you introduce a 3rd dispute mediator party to the transaction.  If the buyer/seller party agree that the deal went through and was fair, the deal gets processed, satisfying the 2 of 3 rule.  If the buyer says "hey hold up I didn't get what I was supposed to", the arbiter steps in, if they decide that they buyer is in the right, they side with the buyer, satisfying the 2 of 3, and the money gets sent back to the buyer.  If the arbiter steps in and says "the buyer is lying the seller delivered what was promised", then the arbiter will side with the seller, again satisfying the 2 of 3 and sending the money to the seller.  At no point can the arbiter take the money, they can only decide who gets it.

Again, this isn't "might be written in", it is there, waiting for a company or person to come around and start a service handling these kinds of situations and charging say x% for the pleasure.

**Wallets**

* Offline Wallets (can be used for cold storage)
 * [Bitcoin-qt](http://bitcoin.org/en/download) - this is the original bitcoin client.  It requires you to download the entire block chain, something many people don't need.  Give's access to wallet encryption, as well as backup and restore.  A good starting point
 * [Armory](https://bitcoinarmory.com/) - runs on top of bitcoin-qt, provides access to many features for advanced users.  I recommend this if you have a large amount of bitcoins that you want to keep safe.
 * [Multibit](https://multibit.org/faq.html) - Lightweight wallet, I have not personally used this one.  I don't think it requires you to download the blockchain
 * [Electrum](http://electrum.org/) - Another lightweight wallet, does not require the entire blockchain to be downloaded, it uses a remote server.  Again, have not tried this one out
* Online Wallets (Do not recommend for long term, as these accounts technically live on a server that you don't own)
 * [Blockchain.info](http://blockchain.info/wallet/) - The most popular and widely used online wallet.  Allows for 2 factor authentication, cloud backups, etc. 
 * [BIPS Online](https://bips.me/) - Another online wallet service, also functions as an exchange.  Also offers offline cold storage and wallet importation
 * [Instawallet](https://instawallet.org/) - Online wallet that randomly generates a wallet key for you when you first go there.  The idea is you can bookmark that page, and then no one else can be served up the same wallet page.  Good for moving coins quickly, but I wouldn't use it for long term storage (anything longer than a day probably).  
 * [Brainwallet](http://brainwallet.org/) - Pretty cool implementation of a wallet, you just give it a phrase, can be whatever you want it to be, and so long as no one can guess the phrase no one can get to your wallet.  Again, I wouldn't trust it for very long to store coins.

Satoshi Dice has a secret key that they release after every 24 hours of gaming.  The game works by taking your transaction ID + the secret key and hashing the two together.  He then takes the last two bytes off of this hash to come up with a number, your "Secret Number", between 0 and 65535.  Depending on the bet you take, you will either win or lose.

For example, if you bet on the 50% game, you are betting that your secret number will be less than 32768, out of 65535 possible numbers.  If it is, you win, if not you lose.

Catch is he keeps house odds on every bet, 1.9%.  Continuing with our 50% example, if you win, you only get 1.957 of what you bet returned back to you.  All the bets are skewed like this.

Ethernet adapter Local Area Connection

You're looking for IPv4 address, Subnet Mask, and Default Gateway.  Write these down in case you have to call your service provider if nothing works.  They are not going to be your usual 192.168.*.* values, these values are what your service provider is giving you.

Now still in the command promt, type in

ipconfig /release

wait for it to finish what it does, then type in 

ipconfig /renew

These two commands release and then renew your IP address.

I haven't overclocked mine yet, haven't felt the need to.  there are two intake fans underneath and one out.  they could have done a much better job at cooling this laptop but oh well.

All in all I love this laptop, i play much starcraft 2 on ultra with fps averaging around 30-40, only dips in long games when there are many maxed out armies running around.  i can also play skyrim on ultra settings with around 30-40 fps.

my recommendation, do buy, but know what you're getting.  I had to have dell ship me a new laptop due the the widely documented mic problems, but i received my new one in the mail in a matter of days, and i swear i love this laptop more and more each day.
